title: The Great Run
text: The river turns silver with salmon. The fish are so thick you could nearly walk across. Every hand is needed.

choices.label: Send every available adult to the river.
choices.followupText: The haul is enormous. Baskets overflow with fish. The people work through the night.

choices.label: Fish steadily while others continue regular duties.
choices.followupText: A good catch, taken without exhausting the community.

choices.label: Hold a ceremony of gratitude at the river's edge.
choices.followupText: The ritual honors the river. Spirit rises. The fish seem plentiful for seasons to come.

title: Unexpected Cold
text: A bitter wind sweeps down from the mountains early. Ice forms on the river's edge. This cold came before anyone expected it.

choices.label: Drop everything and gather firewood.
choices.followupText: The extra work strains the community, but the woodpiles grow tall.

choices.label: Share what firewood exists, rationing carefully.
choices.followupText: Huddled together, the people keep each other warm. Trust deepens.

title: A Lone Traveler
text: A lone figure appears at the edge of camp — weathered, carrying little. They speak a tongue only some of your people can follow. Their eyes are wary but not hostile.

choices.label: Welcome them, share food, and learn what you can.
choices.followupText: The stranger shares knowledge of trails to the south and a good fishing spot two days walk. A small gift for a small meal.

choices.label: Offer water but keep your distance until they move on.
choices.followupText: They rest and leave at dawn. No harm done. No bond made.

choices.label: Invite them to stay and join the community.
choices.followupText: They stay. The community grows by one — a skilled hand who learns the local ways quickly.

title: The River Rises
text: Snowmelt swells the river beyond its banks. Low-lying storage and paths are threatened. The water rises quickly.

choices.label: Move stored food to higher ground immediately.
choices.followupText: Exhausting work, but the stores are saved. The river claims only mud.

choices.label: Build a quick earthen berm to redirect water.
choices.followupText: The berm holds. People cheer as the water turns aside. The tools wear down, but the effort unites.

choices.label: Wait — the river has flooded before and always receded.
choices.followupText: The water reaches the storage pits. Several baskets of food are lost. The mood is sour.

title: A Sickness Moves Through Camp
text: First one adult, then three more — a fever that leaves people weak and shivering for days. The elders recognize it as a seasonal illness, dangerous if untreated.

choices.label: Rest the sick, have elders tend them with herbs.
choices.followupText: Recovery is slow but full. The healers' skill is renewed. The sick remember who tended them.

choices.label: Quarantine the ill to protect the rest.
choices.followupText: The isolation works — sickness does not spread. But those quarantined feel abandoned.

choices.label: Hold a healing ceremony for strength.
choices.followupText: The ceremony lifts spirits. Some of the sick seem to recover faster than expected.

title: Berries Beyond Count
text: The hillsides are purple and red with ripe berries. More than the people have seen in years. The children are already eating.

choices.label: Gather as much as possible — fill every basket.
choices.followupText: Baskets overflow. The people will eat well and have some to dry.

choices.label: Gather plenty, but also teach the children the proper way.
choices.followupText: A slower harvest, but the children learn which plants to pick and which to leave. A good day.

title: The Tools Give Out
text: Blades chip. Handles split. The season's work has worn the community's tools down past usefulness. Something must be done.

choices.label: Spend time and firewood crafting new tools.
choices.followupText: New blades, scrapers, and handles. The work goes slowly at first, then with pride.

choices.label: Trade some stored food for tools from a passing group.
choices.followupText: A fair trade. The strangers seem pleased. A small alliance forms.

choices.label: Manage with what you have — improvise.
choices.followupText: The people make do. But cracked tools slow everything down.

title: The Great Bear
text: A large brown bear has been raiding drying racks and scattering food caches. It moves boldly, showing no fear. The hunters debate what to do.

choices.label: Drive it off with fire and noise.
choices.followupText: The bear retreats to the forest. The people feel capable. It may return, but not tonight.

choices.label: Hunt and kill the bear.
choices.followupText: A dangerous but successful hunt. The meat feeds many. The hunters gain respect.

choices.label: Relocate caches and avoid confrontation — the forest belongs to both.
choices.followupText: The elders approve. The people adapt. The bear is not seen again at camp.

title: The Elder Speaks
text: The oldest elder calls a gathering. She says she has lived through enough winters to know something the young forget: the land speaks, if you learn to listen. She offers to teach.

choices.label: Have the young adults sit with her for several days.
choices.followupText: The sessions are long and sometimes quiet. But knowledge passes. Skills sharpen.

choices.label: Honor her with a meal and listen to her story.
choices.followupText: Her story spans decades. The people sit in silence, then talk long into the night.

title: The Dry Summer
text: Weeks pass without rain. The river drops low. Fish grow scarce in the shallow water. Berries shrivel before ripening.

choices.label: Push harder on hunting to compensate.
choices.followupText: The hunters range farther and work harder. Food is found, but the people are tired.

choices.label: Ration and reduce consumption this season.
choices.followupText: The people go a little hungry, but the stores grow. A hard discipline.

choices.label: Hold a rain ceremony and trust in the turning of seasons.
choices.followupText: No rain comes from the ceremony, but the people's hearts are steadied. They endure together.

title: Hidden Waters
text: A child following a deer trail stumbles onto a hidden lake, thick with fish. She runs back breathless to tell the adults.

choices.label: Send fishing crews immediately.
choices.followupText: The lake yields an extraordinary haul. The child who found it is celebrated.

choices.label: Mark the location carefully and return next season.
choices.followupText: Patience. The location is recorded. This will feed the people for seasons to come.

title: Territorial Tension
text: A group from the river's other side has been fishing the same pools. No words have been exchanged, but there are hard looks. A confrontation may come.

choices.label: Approach them and propose shared fishing times.
choices.followupText: After tense negotiation, an agreement is reached. The river is large enough. Trust begins.

choices.label: Mark your boundaries firmly and hold them.
choices.followupText: The other group withdraws, but the tension lingers. No one feels fully safe.

choices.label: Give them a gift of food and open a conversation.
choices.followupText: Generosity disarms them. They are surprised. A fragile friendship takes its first breath.

title: The Gifted Child
text: One of the older children shows unusual skill — she has been quietly imitating the fishers, and her catches from the shallows outshine some adults.

choices.label: Formally begin her apprenticeship with the best fisher.
choices.followupText: She takes to it immediately. The community watches with pride.

choices.label: Let her develop naturally — no need to rush.
choices.followupText: She continues on her own path. There is wisdom in not forcing the gift.

title: The Dark Bird
text: A large black bird has perched on the lodge roof for three days and will not leave. The elders disagree about what it means. Unease settles on the camp.

choices.label: Hold a ceremony to acknowledge whatever is coming.
choices.followupText: The bird leaves at dawn after the ceremony. The people feel watched over, not threatened.

choices.label: Shoo it away and focus on practical winter work.
choices.followupText: The bird goes. The elders are quiet. Extra firewood is gathered. Practical minds prevail.

title: Abundance of Fall
text: The cedars, oaks, and berry bushes have given more than usual. Roots are plentiful. It is a rare season of quiet abundance.

choices.label: Gather and preserve as much as possible.
choices.followupText: The stores overflow. Winter looks far less frightening.

choices.label: Hold a feast and share the surplus with morale in mind.
choices.followupText: A night of dancing, story, and full bellies. The people remember this for seasons.

title: The Long Night
text: The coldest night anyone can remember. Children press close. Elders shiver. The fire must be kept alive through the dark hours.

choices.label: Burn extra firewood through the night.
choices.followupText: All survive. The warmth is remembered. Firewood runs lower, but spirits hold.

choices.label: Huddle together with minimal fire, sharing body heat.
choices.followupText: A long, hard night. But the people discover how much they trust each other.

title: First Thaw
text: The ice breaks. The birds return first, then the insects, then the first green shoots. After the winter, the world smells alive again. The children run into the meadow.

choices.label: Begin planting and renewal tasks immediately.
choices.followupText: The work feels light. Spring brings energy that winter stole.

choices.label: Rest and celebrate survival before the labor begins.
choices.followupText: A day of play and rest. The people needed this. They return to work with full hearts.

title: A Better Way
text: An experienced fisher has been experimenting with a new design — a weir made of woven branches that channels fish into pools. It worked. She shows the community.

choices.label: Build the weir and adopt the technique.
choices.followupText: The weir works beautifully. Fish yields improve significantly. An innovation remembered.

choices.label: Observe and let her refine it further before committing.
choices.followupText: She continues her experiments. Progress is slower, but the design improves.

title: Discontent
text: Voices rise in camp. Some feel the labor is unfair — that some work harder while others take more. The community is fractured by a quiet argument.

choices.label: Hold a council — let everyone speak.
choices.followupText: It is a long, difficult evening. But grievances aired are grievances eased. People feel heard.

choices.label: Acknowledge the issue and adjust duties publicly.
choices.followupText: The adjustment isn't perfect, but it shows leadership. Tensions cool.

choices.label: A hard season demands hard choices — maintain current course.
choices.followupText: The discontent festers. People work but resent it. Something will need to give.

title: The Ancient Cedar Grove
text: Scouts return from the hills with news: a grove of enormous red cedars, their trunks wider than three people with arms outstretched. The wood is extraordinary.

choices.label: Harvest timber carefully for building.
choices.followupText: The cedar is remarkable. It will build lodges and tools for years.

choices.label: Mark the grove as sacred — do not harvest it.
choices.followupText: The elders weep with gratitude. The grove becomes a place of ceremony. Its roots hold the community.

title: The Silver Morning
text: An early morning mist parts to reveal the river thick with fish — more than anyone has seen in a single day. The window may not last long.

choices.label: Drop everything and fish all morning.
choices.followupText: An astonishing haul. The people will eat well for weeks.

choices.label: Fish efficiently and return to regular duties by midday.
choices.followupText: A good morning's work. The rest of the day proceeds normally.

title: The Longest Night
text: The sun sets early. By nightfall, the darkness is complete and total. The elders say this night is a threshold: what is spoken into the dark shapes the year to come.

choices.label: Hold an all-night vigil of song and story.
choices.followupText: By dawn, the people are tired but transformed. Something has been passed down.

choices.label: Sleep early and rise refreshed for the work ahead.
choices.followupText: Practical rest. The elders say nothing. The night passes quietly.

title: A Hunter Falls
text: A promising hunter misjudged a hillside and twisted his leg badly. He will not be mobile for the rest of the season. The community must adapt.

choices.label: Redistribute his duties and tend his recovery fully.
choices.followupText: His recovery is complete. The community's care leaves no one forgotten.

choices.label: Push others harder to cover the shortfall.
choices.followupText: The work gets done, but the people are exhausted and resentful.

title: Stones of the Ancestors
text: Workers clearing a hillside uncover an arrangement of stones unlike any natural formation. The elders grow quiet when they see it.

choices.label: Restore and protect the site.
choices.followupText: The stones are carefully reset. The elders hold ceremony there that night. The land remembers.

choices.label: Record it, but continue the clearing work.
choices.followupText: Work continues. The elders say little. Some things cannot be undone.
